# How to translate this chunk

This file holds `items`, a list of `{"k", "ctx", "t"}`. `t` is English text
that a reader of an Indian app or website sees. `ctx` is the field it came
from, such as label, hint, button, documents, brief or title. Use it to judge
tone and length: a label stays short, a hint can be a sentence.

Write `{"items": [{"k": ..., "t": ...}, ...]}` to the path in `write_to`.
Keep every `k` unchanged and in the same order. Put the translation in `t`.
Leave out `ctx`. Do not add, merge, split or drop items.

## Keep these exactly as they are

- Placeholders and markup: `{0}`, `{name}`, `%s`, `%d`, `%1$s`, HTML tags, `\n`.
- Website addresses, e-mail addresses and links.
- Every number: phone and toll-free numbers, Aadhaar, account, IFSC, PAN, PIN
  codes, amounts, dates, percentages. Write digits as 0-9, the Western digits,
  in every language, including Urdu. People type these into forms that take
  Western digits.
- Acronyms people know in Latin letters: OTP, PAN, IFSC, UPI, KYC, e-KYC, DBT,
  BPL, APL, NFSA, PM-KISAN, SMS, PDF, ID.

## Names

- Product, app, portal and scheme names: transliterate them into the script so
  they read naturally. Keep any acronym inside them in Latin, so "APPSC
  portal" becomes APPSC followed by the word for portal.
- A button or menu label quoted from a website, such as 'Apply Online' or
  'Register', stays in English inside quotes. The reader has to find that exact
  English word on the screen.
- People and places in examples are transliterated, never replaced with other
  names.
- Government office titles are transliterated so the reader can say them at
  the counter: Tahsildar, Patwari, Talathi, Mamlatdar, BDO, Collector, Gram
  Panchayat. The language notes below give the usual local forms.

## Tone

Write for an ordinary person who may be elderly and may have had little
schooling. Use everyday spoken language, not heavy official vocabulary. Where
people really say the English word, write it in the script: online, form,
portal, login, mobile, bank, certificate, download, upload, app. Keep
instructions short and direct, in the form "do this".

"Gender" means sex (male or female). It is never the word for caste.

## Before you write

Check that you have the same number of items as the input and that every
number and placeholder came through. Write the whole file in ONE Write call,
as valid UTF-8 JSON with no `\u` escapes and nothing else in the file.

सर्टिफिकेट, डाउनलोड, अपलोड.

Gender: लिंग (never जाति). Money: रु. 6,000; रु. 8 लाख. September: सितंबर.

Palanhar Yojana (support for orphan and needy children)
Social Justice & Empowerment Department, Government of Rajasthan

Pays a monthly amount to the relative or guardian (the palanhar) who brings up an orphan, or a child in a listed hardship category, at home, so the child stays with family and keeps studying. Orphans get Rs 1,500 a month up to age 6 and Rs 2,500 from 6 to 18; other categories get Rs 750 and Rs 1,500, and most families also get Rs 2,000 a year for books, clothes and shoes. You apply online at an e-Mitra kiosk, through SSO or on the Palanhar app with face authentication, and renew every July.
Rs 750 to Rs 2,500 a month per child, plus Rs 2,000 a year
Child under 18 (up to 19 if still in Class 12 or below), enrolled at an Anganwadi (age 0–6) or a school (6–18)
Orphans; children of parents sentenced to death or life imprisonment; children of a widow or a divorced or abandoned woman who gets a pension; children of a remarried widow
Children of parents with HIV/AIDS, leprosy, silicosis or 40% or more disability, and children of a mother who has gone in nata (widow and nata categories: up to 3 children)
Palanhar family income up to Rs 1.20 lakh a year; no income proof needed for BPL, Astha or Antyodaya card holders and widow, divorced, abandoned or disability pensioners
Palanhar is a Rajasthan native or has lived in the state at least 3 years; an adult brother or sister can be the palanhar
Stops if the palanhar takes a government job or family income crosses the limit
Jan Aadhaar card of the palanhar, with the child added to it
Residence proof — domicile certificate, ration card or voter ID (not needed for BPL, Astha, Antyodaya, PDS or pension holders)

Anganwadi registration or school study certificate (not needed if the school has verified the child on Shala Darpan)

Choose the one category that fits; the amount and the proof needed depend on it.
As on the child's Aadhaar card.

Mukhya Mantri Jeevan Raksha Kosh and SSIAF (Referral Treatment Help)
Health & Family Welfare Department, Government of Sikkim

If the State Medical Board refers a Sikkimese patient for treatment that Sikkim cannot give, the state pays up to Rs.2 lakh. You get cashless treatment at listed hospitals in Delhi, Kolkata, Siliguri, Vellore, Mumbai and inside Sikkim, or a reimbursement. BPL patients first get Rs.1.5 lakh under the Sikkim State Illness Assistance Fund (SSIAF), then another Rs.1.5 lakh from this fund, Rs.3 lakh in all. Regular government servants and their dependants are not covered. Since a 2022 amendment the rules are also called the Mukhya Mantri Swasthya Suvidha Yojana (MMSSY).
Up to Rs.2 lakh for referred treatment; up to Rs.3 lakh for BPL patients
Holder of a Sikkim Subject Certificate or Certificate of Identification (COI), or a family on the state BPL list
Referred by the State Medical Board for treatment outside Sikkim or at an empanelled hospital
Regular government servants and their dependants are not covered
Patients under 20 qualify through their birth certificate and the father's SSC or COI. A woman married to an SSC or COI holder needs her own COI and a marriage certificate

Sikkim Aama Sashaktikaran Yojana (Aama Yojana)
Women, Child, Senior Citizen and Divyangjan Welfare Department, Government of Sikkim

Mothers in Sikkim who have no job get Rs.40,000 a year, paid in two instalments of Rs.20,000 straight into their own bank account through the State Bank of Sikkim. It started in 2021-22 as the Aama Yojana at Rs.20,000 a year. It was later renamed and the amount doubled. Married, unmarried, widowed, divorced and separated mothers can all get it. You collect the form at your Block Development Office, the Gram Sabha or Ward Sabha passes your name, and officials check it before the money is released.

Rs 1,000 every month, paid into the bank account, for boys who studied Classes 6 to 12 in a Tamil Nadu government school or a government-aided Tamil-medium school and have joined college. It is the boys' version of Pudhumai Penn, started in August 2024, and is paid until the first degree, diploma or ITI course is finished, on top of other scholarships. You apply through your college, which enters your details on the UMIS portal.

Chief Minister's Comprehensive Health Insurance Scheme (CMCHIS Card)
Health and Family Welfare Department, Tamil Nadu Health Systems Project (TNHSP)

Free, cashless hospital treatment for low-income families in Tamil Nadu, at government hospitals and empanelled private hospitals, up to Rs 5 lakh per family a year. In Tamil Nadu it runs together with Ayushman Bharat PM-JAY (CMCHIS-PMJAY), so one card covers both. In August 2026 the Chief Minister announced that the yearly cover will rise to Rs 25 lakh; ask the helpline whether the higher cover has started. You enrol once, at the CMCHIS card centre in the District Collector's office.
Up to Rs 5 lakh a year per family, cashless (Rs 25 lakh cover announced in August 2026)
Annual family income below Rs 1,20,000, certified by the Village Administrative Officer (VAO)
The family holds a Tamil Nadu ration (smart family) card, and everyone to be covered is named on it
Covers the head of the family, the legal spouse, children and dependent parents

Some groups join with their own ID card instead of an income certificate: differently-abled card holders, old-age and widow pensioners, handloom workers' board members, recognised journalists, transgender persons, Sri Lankan Tamil refugees and orphans
There is no age limit, and the family pays no premium
Income certificate from the VAO showing a yearly family income under Rs 1,20,000 (the VAO can also sign the box on the form itself)
Aadhaar cards of the head of the family and of the members to be covered
